authority.distribution: macOS with Xcode Command Line Tools
authority.note: runtime pins follow the repository oracle 体例 (conformance/oracles/java-properties-v1/README.md: the manifest is frozen after the adapter is executed on the authoritative runtime). The macOS-leg golden outputs (converted-byte digests) are enforced as plutil-vs-Swift-driver byte identity plus reparse and value equality at runtime; byte-level golden digests are frozen by the first pinned-macOS run and must be updated together with the runtime pins only when the pinned toolchain changes. Honest scope (G113, 2026-08-13): no macOS execution exists in any repository — the macOS runtime pins below are declarations taken from the Apple system-requirements/release-notes pages, not observed facts; they become observed facts at the first pinned-macOS run.

runtime.macos_observation: not-yet-executed as of 2026-08-13 (declared, not observed; see the authority note)
runtime.windows_build_note: development machine of the plistlib secondary leg (Windows); not a macOS runtime fact

driver.transport: ASCII TSV; lowercase UTF-8 hex for strings, lowercase hex for bytes and IEEE 754 bit patterns; deterministic value dump (dictionary entries sorted by hex key, arrays in source order)

plistlib.role: secondary structural cross-check only; never the semantic authority (RFC 0013 §13; plan §6.3)

adapter.transport: ASCII TSV; lowercase UTF-8 hex for strings, lowercase hex for bytes and IEEE 754 bit patterns; deterministic value dump (dictionary entries sorted by key, arrays in source order)

comparison.scope: parse/convert/value outcomes on the pinned macOS runner only; Apple behavior is the differential authority (RFC 0013 §13)
comparison.cross_oracle: for every expected-ok conversion direction, plutil and the Swift driver must produce byte-identical output (both invoke the same Foundation writer); converted bytes must re-lint cleanly with plutil and reparse with the driver
comparison.values: plutil -p of the fixture equals (sorted-line multiset, because Foundation does not guarantee NSDictionary iteration order) plutil -p of every successfully converted file; the Swift driver's deterministic value dump must match exactly across the same files
comparison.plistlib_leg: secondary structural cross-check only (scripts/run-plistlib-oracle.ps1): profile detection plus a deterministic value dump compared by value-sha256 against the pins below; plistlib is never the semantic authority (RFC 0013 §13)
comparison.consema_counterpart: the fixture set contains only Complete-under-Consema inputs; Consema Complete maps to lint ok here. Recovered/FatalFormationFailure Consema inputs are not part of this fixture set; where Consema deliberately diverges from Foundation, the divergence is recorded in the exclusion inventory below and a differential disagreement can never be resolved by changing Consema behavior (RFC 0013 §13, plan §6.3)

divergence_inventory.name: UTF-32 BOM and unknown declared encodings
divergence_inventory.oracle: Foundation additionally recognizes UTF-32 BOMs and unknown declared encodings through IANA lookup
divergence_inventory.consema: follows RFC 0012's stricter source contract: UTF-8/UTF-16LE/UTF-16BE only, UTF-16 requires a BOM (RFC 0013 §2.1)

divergence_inventory.name: Duplicate keys: silent last-wins vs preservation
divergence_inventory.oracle: Foundation replaces silently (last wins) through CFDictionarySetValue; plutil -p and the parsed value show only the last occurrence
divergence_inventory.consema: duplicate keys are accepted as ordered native facts with independent association identity; never collapsed (RFC 0013 §4.4, §5.9)

divergence_inventory.name: Strict base64
divergence_inventory.oracle: Foundation silently skips non-alphabet characters and tolerates missing padding
divergence_inventory.consema: standard alphabet, ASCII whitespace between characters only, padding exactly as required; any other character is Recovered (RFC 0013 §4.8)

divergence_inventory.name: Strict version attribute
divergence_inventory.oracle: Foundation ignores element attributes entirely
divergence_inventory.consema: root requires version="1.0" exactly; missing, different, or additional attributes are Recovered (RFC 0013 §4.2)

divergence_inventory.name: Strict DOCTYPE
divergence_inventory.oracle: Foundation skips any DOCTYPE without validating it
divergence_inventory.consema: DOCTYPE must be exactly the Apple plist identifier; other names, identifiers, internal subsets, or external-only DOCTYPEs are Recovered (RFC 0013 §4.1)

divergence_inventory.name: Trailing content rejection
divergence_inventory.oracle: Foundation ignores trailing garbage after </plist> entirely
divergence_inventory.consema: only whitespace, comments, and processing instructions are admitted after </plist>; any other bytes are Recovered (RFC 0013 §4.10)

divergence_inventory.name: Calendar validation
divergence_inventory.oracle: Foundation normalizes out-of-range date fields through the Gregorian calendar
divergence_inventory.consema: calendar fields must be valid (month 1-12, day valid for month and year, hour 0-23, minute and second 0-59); invalid fields are Recovered (RFC 0013 §4.7)

divergence_inventory.name: 64-bit integer range
divergence_inventory.oracle: Foundation additionally accepts magnitudes up to 128-bit
divergence_inventory.consema: v1 freezes the signed 64-bit range; wider magnitudes are Recovered (RFC 0013 §4.5, §6). Plan R-1: fixtures must not contain 0x14 16-byte integer inputs (SInt128 non-inclusion), and any plutil output wider than 64 bits is excluded from the fixture set at generation time

divergence_inventory.name: bplist01 header rejection
divergence_inventory.oracle: Foundation's reader accepts bplist01 and later tolerated bplist0?
divergence_inventory.consema: v1 freezes the exact header bplist00; any other version string is Recovered (RFC 0013 §5.1)

divergence_inventory.name: 16-byte integer marker rejection
divergence_inventory.oracle: Foundation reads the 0x14 marker (16-byte integer) of newer format versions
divergence_inventory.consema: 0x14 is a v1 exclusion: Recovered with a stable diagnostic (RFC 0013 §5.2)

divergence_inventory.name: null marker rejection
divergence_inventory.oracle: Foundation reads the 0x00 null marker of newer format versions
divergence_inventory.consema: null is a v1 exclusion (the XML representation has no null element, so the profiles could not share that value); Recovered (RFC 0013 §5.2)

divergence_inventory.name: Non-finite date payload rejection
divergence_inventory.oracle: Foundation constructs a CFDate from a non-finite 0x33 payload
divergence_inventory.consema: a non-finite date payload is Recovered; date values must be finite (RFC 0013 §5.5)

divergence_inventory.name: ASCII-string high-bit byte rejection
divergence_inventory.oracle: Foundation maps bytes with the high bit set through kCFStringEncodingASCII's Latin-1-compatible behavior
divergence_inventory.consema: every byte of an ASCII string must be below 0x80; a high-bit byte is Recovered (RFC 0013 §5.6)

divergence_inventory.name: Non-string binary dictionary keys
divergence_inventory.oracle: Foundation accepts any non-container key, and then cannot write such a dictionary to XML
divergence_inventory.consema: dictionary keys must be strings in v1; non-string keys are Recovered at formation so both profiles share exactly one dictionary key contract (RFC 0013 §5.9)

divergence_inventory.name: CR-containing strings
divergence_inventory.oracle: Foundation's plist parser passes raw CR through string content
divergence_inventory.consema: XML 1.0 line-end normalization applies to native text (raw CR and CRLF become LF), per RFC 0012; recorded divergence for fixtures containing CR inside strings (RFC 0013 §4.9)

divergence_inventory.name: Stricter offset-table entry bounds
divergence_inventory.oracle: Foundation checks only off < offsetTableOffset and forces the range check only for the top object
divergence_inventory.consema: every offset-table entry and the top object's offset must lie in [8, offsetTableOffset); fixture generation must not rely on Foundation behavior to infer bounds (RFC 0013 §5.11, plan R-11)

divergence_inventory.name: Apple-writer key sorting
divergence_inventory.oracle: Apple's writer sorts dictionary keys with CFStringCompare
divergence_inventory.consema: canonical materialization preserves input association order; sorting is representation style, not a value fact (RFC 0013 §10.1, §15)

divergence_inventory.name: 0x0F fill byte
divergence_inventory.oracle: Foundation's reader tolerates the 0x0F fill byte
divergence_inventory.consema: 0x0F is a v1 exclusion: Recovered. Writing must confirm plutil output never contains 0x0F (RFC 0013 §5.2, plan R-3)

divergence_inventory.name: plistlib/Foundation three-way divergences
divergence_inventory.oracle: plistlib diverges from Foundation on the UID upper bound, the 0x0F fill byte, and the extended-size marker
divergence_inventory.consema: RFC freezes Foundation behavior; plistlib is a secondary structural cross-check only and never the semantic authority. Its divergences never enter the differential comparison (RFC 0013 §13, plan R-2)

divergence_inventory.name: Shared object identity XML conversion
divergence_inventory.oracle: converts the shared reference silently, duplicating the shared object in XML
divergence_inventory.consema: shared object identity is a binary-only fact; conversion to XML fails atomically under hard gate 3 (RFC 0013 §7)
divergence_inventory.kind: exclusion (conversion leg: Foundation succeeds, Consema refuses by design)

divergence_inventory.name: UID XML-inexpressibility
divergence_inventory.oracle: Foundation refuses to write a UID-bearing dictionary as XML (equivalent outcome)
divergence_inventory.consema: UID values are binary-only; conversion to XML fails atomically under hard gate 3 (RFC 0013 §7, §15)
divergence_inventory.kind: exclusion (equivalent outcome: both oracles refuse the conversion)

shape_level: converted-byte shape: the differential compares plutil output against the Swift driver output (same Foundation writer); it never compares against Consema canonical materialization bytes, which are pinned by the conformance vectors (RFC 0013 §10)
value-dump line order: Foundation NSDictionary hash order is not guaranteed, so the Swift driver sorts dictionary keys before dumping and the plutil -p comparison is sorted-line multiset equality
real/date text spelling (plan R-4): canonical real spellings (nan/inf vs NaN/Infinity) are measured against pinned plutil -convert xml1 output by the M7 materialization gate, not by this oracle
application_layer: NSKeyedArchiver object-graph reconstruction ($objects/$class tables) is out of scope (RFC 0013 §15); fixtures verify UID value preservation only
old-style ASCII (NeXTSTEP) plists are out of scope (RFC 0013 §15)
preference domains, defaults(1), and any other application-layer plist consumption are out of scope (RFC 0013 §15)
the plistlib leg is a structural cross-check only; its three-way divergences from Foundation (D-19) mean it is never the semantic authority
exclusions.policy: a differential disagreement cannot be resolved by changing Consema behavior without an RFC, and no untracked allowlist exists (RFC 0013 §13; plan §6.3)

skip_path: when the runner is not macOS, the wrapper exits with code 3 and the manifest records the allowed skip (plan R-15, mirroring conformance/oracles/hcl-go-v1/manifest.json); the suite id remains consema.plist.macos-differential@1. The plistlib runner runs wherever the pinned CPython exists; when the pinned CPython exists but the Windows build does not match the pin, the wrapper prints an explicit skip message and exits with code 3 (2026-08-14 波 3 audit: the previous wording denying this skip path was corrected here, mirroring conformance/oracles/plist-macos-v1/README.md)
